examples.en: The children are playing in the room, giggling.
The baby giggles when she sees her mom.

examples.ko: 친구들이 뭐가 그렇게 재미있는지 계속 까르르거려요.
examples.en: My friends keep giggling, as if something is really funny.

examples.ko: 밤늦게 까르르거리는 소리가 들려서 잠을 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up because I heard giggling late at night.
My nephew giggled as he was tickled.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에는 너무 까르르거리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't giggle too much during class.

explain: 웃음소리가 계속 이어지는 모습을 보여 줘요. '까르르 웃다'처럼 풀어서 말해도 뜻이 같아요. 주로 아이나 친구들끼리 즐겁게 웃을 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It shows the laughter continuing over time. Saying '까르르 웃다' instead means the same thing. It suits children or friends laughing happily together.

examples.en: I'm sleepy and keep blinking slowly.
The child looked at me, blinking.
The fluorescent light is flickering and my eyes hurt.
The cow is blinking its big eyes.
He just blinked, as if he didn't understand.
The light flickered and then went out.

explain: '깜박거리다'의 큰말이라서 눈이나 불빛이 크고 느릿하게 깜빡이는 느낌이에요. 눈을 감았다 뜨는 모습뿐 아니라 불빛이 꺼질 듯 말 듯할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is the 'larger' counterpart of '깜박거리다', giving a big, slow blinking feel. It describes eyes opening and closing, and also lights flickering on the verge of going out.

examples.en: I was startled by a sudden sound out of nowhere.
A friend showed up at my house out of the blue.

examples.ko: 갑자기 그런 말을 하다니 좀 난데없어요.
examples.en: Saying something like that suddenly is a bit out of the blue.

examples.ko: 그날 난데없던 전화 한 통이 모든 걸 바꿨어요.
examples.en: One unexpected phone call that day changed everything.

examples.ko: 난데없을 수도 있지만, 저와 같이 여행 갈래요?
examples.en: This may be out of the blue, but do you want to travel with me?

examples.ko: 난데없게 들리겠지만 사실은 오래 생각한 일이에요.
examples.en: It may sound sudden, but I have actually thought about it for a long time.

explain: '갑자기'보다 어디서 왔는지 모를 만큼 뜻밖이라는 느낌이 강해요. 형용사지만 '난데없는 N'과 '난데없이' 모양으로 가장 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 조용하던 회의에서 난데없이 홍두깨처럼 해고 이야기가 나왔어요.
phrases.en: In the quiet meeting, talk of layoffs came up completely out of the blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 뜻밖의 일이나 엉뚱한 말이 불쑥 나올 때 쓰는 표현이에요. 보통 당황스럽거나 어이없는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for when something unexpected or off-the-wall suddenly pops up. It is usually used for confusing or baffling situations.

explain_en: Compared with '갑자기', it feels more like something came from nowhere. It is an adjective, but it is used most often as '난데없는 + noun' and '난데없이'.

examples.en: He answered with his eyes lowered, perhaps out of shyness.

examples.ko: 눈을 내리깔지 말고 저를 보고 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't look down; look at me and speak.
The child lowered his gaze, afraid of being scolded.

examples.ko: 목소리를 내리깔며 조용히 말하니 더 무섭게 들렸어요.
examples.en: He spoke quietly in a low voice, and it sounded even scarier.

examples.ko: 눈을 내리깔아 바닥만 쳐다보는 모습이 안쓰러웠어요.
examples.en: It was pitiful to see him staring only at the floor with his eyes cast down.

examples.ko: 발표할 때 눈을 내리깔면 자신 없어 보여요.
examples.en: If you keep your eyes lowered when presenting, you look unsure of yourself.

explain: '고개를 숙이다'는 머리를 숙이는 것이고, '눈을 내리깔다'는 고개와 상관없이 시선만 아래로 두는 거예요. 수줍거나 눈치를 볼 때도 쓰고, 상대를 깔보듯 볼 때도 써요. '목소리를 내리깔다'는 목소리를 낮고 굵게 낼 때 써요.
explain_en: '고개를 숙이다' means bowing your head, while '눈을 내리깔다' is lowering only your gaze, whether or not your head moves. It is used when shy or wary of others' reactions, and also when looking down on someone. '목소리를 내리깔다' is for speaking in a low, deep voice.

examples.ko: 동생은 거짓말을 해 놓고도 능청스럽게 웃고 있었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling had lied but was smiling with a perfectly innocent face.

examples.ko: 시치미 떼는 모습이 어찌나 능청스러운지 화를 낼 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: The way he feigned ignorance was so bold that I couldn't even get angry.

examples.ko: 그는 아무것도 모르는 척 능청을 떨었어요.
examples.en: He played innocent as if he knew nothing.
His acting innocent was so good that everyone was fooled.

examples.ko: 아버지는 능청 섞인 농담으로 분위기를 풀어 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father eased the mood with a deadpan joke.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 능청스러운 연기로 관객을 웃겼어요.
examples.en: That actor made the audience laugh with his deadpan acting.

explain: '능청을 떨다', '능청을 부리다'처럼 써요. 알면서 모르는 척하는 태도인데, 밉기보다 얄밉거나 웃기다는 느낌일 때가 많아요. 비슷한 '시치미(를) 떼다'는 행동 자체를 말하고, '능청'은 그 태연한 태도에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It is used in '능청을 떨다' or '능청을 부리다'. It describes acting as if you don't know something you actually know, and the feeling is often more cheeky or funny than truly hateful. The similar '시치미(를) 떼다' names the act of feigning ignorance, while '능청' focuses on the calm, innocent-looking attitude.

examples.ko: 퇴근 시간에는 지하철 안에서 사람들에게 밀려다녀요.
examples.en: During rush hour, I get pushed around by people on the subway.

examples.ko: 시장이 너무 붐벼서 이리저리 밀려다니다가 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: The market was so crowded that I got pushed this way and that and lost my way.

examples.ko: 파도에 밀려다니는 작은 배가 불안해 보여요.
examples.en: The little boat being tossed around by the waves looks precarious.

examples.ko: 저는 사람들 틈에서 밀려다니기 싫어서 일찍 갔어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to get shoved around in the crowd, so I went early.
I lost my shoe while being pushed around at the concert hall.
I was shoved around by the crowds, so it was a tiring day.

explain: '밀려가다'가 한 방향으로 떠밀려 가는 느낌이라면, 이 말은 이리저리 계속 떠밀리는 느낌이에요. 사람이 많은 곳이나 파도처럼 힘에 밀려 움직일 때 써요. '떠밀리다'도 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: '밀려가다' feels like being pushed in one direction, while this word suggests being pushed back and forth again and again. It is used for crowds or waves that move you around. '떠밀리다' can be used in a similar way.

examples.ko: 그는 젊을 때 방랑 생활을 오래 했어요.
examples.en: He lived a wandering life for a long time when he was young.
After a long period of wandering, he returned to his hometown.
The poet left a record of his wanderings as a book.

examples.ko: 이제 방랑을 끝내고 한곳에 정착하기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to end my wandering and settle in one place.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 한 청년의 방랑을 그리고 있어요.
examples.en: This novel portrays the wandering of a young man.

examples.ko: 오랜 방랑에도 그는 꿈을 버리지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even after long wandering, he did not give up his dream.

explain: 정해진 곳이나 목적 없이 떠도는 것을 말하고, 돌아올 곳이 정해진 '여행'과는 느낌이 달라요. 주로 글이나 이야기에서 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '떠돌아다니다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes drifting around with no fixed place or purpose, which feels different from a '여행' where you have somewhere to return to. It is mainly used in writing and stories, while in daily talk people say '떠돌아다니다'.

examples.ko: 남의 말에 부화뇌동하지 말고 직접 알아보세요.
examples.en: Don't just follow what others say; find out for yourself.

examples.ko: 친구들이 다 산다고 해서 부화뇌동해서 주식을 샀어요.
examples.en: Everyone said they were buying, so I blindly followed and bought stocks.
He is not someone who just goes along with the mood.
If you blindly follow rumors, you'll regret it later.

examples.ko: 회의에서 다들 부화뇌동하는 바람에 반대 의견이 없었어요.
examples.en: Since everyone just went along in the meeting, there were no opposing opinions.
You should be careful about following the crowd when you invest.

explain: 그냥 '따라 하다'와 달리, 줏대 없이 남에게 휩쓸린다는 비판이 들어 있어요. 보통 '~에 부화뇌동하다'로 쓰고, 칭찬하는 말로는 쓰지 않아요. 말할 때는 '휩쓸리다'나 '남 따라 하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '따라 하다' (to imitate), it carries criticism: following others without a mind of your own. It is usually used as '~에 부화뇌동하다' and never as praise. In casual speech, '휩쓸리다' or '남 따라 하다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: People came out onto the street to watch the fire.
In the old days, people would sometimes crowd over to watch a fire.
Don't look on like a bystander just because it's someone else's problem.

examples.ko: 불구경하는 사람들 때문에 소방차가 못 지나갔어요.
examples.en: The fire truck couldn't get through because of people watching the fire.
It's dangerous, so don't stand and watch the fire. Move far away.
While watching the fire, I saw the firefighters arrive.

explain: 불이 난 것을 구경한다는 말인데, 지금은 '불구경하듯'처럼 남의 어려움을 가만히 보기만 하는 태도를 비유할 때도 많이 써요. 이때는 조금 차갑게 들릴 수 있어요. 실제 화재 때는 위험하니 하지 말라는 말과 함께 나오기도 해요.

phrases.example: 친구가 힘든데 강 건너 불구경하듯 보고만 있었어요.
phrases.en: My friend was struggling and I just stood by watching as if it had nothing to do with me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기와 상관없는 일이라 도와주지 않고 가만히 지켜보는 태도를 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize a person who watches without helping because they treat it as none of their business.

explain_en: It means to watch a fire, but nowadays people often use '불구경하듯' figuratively for just watching someone else's trouble without helping. In that use it can sound a bit cold. For real fires it often comes up in warnings not to do it because it is dangerous.

examples.en: The baby is hungry and keeps shrieking and crying.
Why are you talking in such a shrill voice?
My younger sibling squealed for the toy.
The baby who had been screeching all night finally fell asleep.
Stop shrieking and try speaking slowly.
The baby was screeching, so I couldn't finish the call.

explain: 그냥 '울다'보다 소리가 높고 날카로워서 듣는 사람이 시끄럽다고 느낄 때 써요. 주로 아기나 아이에게 쓰고, 어른에게 쓰면 무례하게 들려요. 소리 내는 모습이 계속될 때 '-거리다' 형태로 자주 써요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '울다' (to cry), the sound is higher and sharper, and the listener finds it noisy. It is mostly used for babies or children; about an adult it sounds rude. The '-거리다' form suggests the noise keeps going.

en: gape; open and close the mouth repeatedly (like a fish)

examples.en: The goldfish in the tank open and close their mouths.
The fish are gulping at the surface of the water.

examples.ko: 아이가 입을 뻐끔거리며 물고기 흉내를 냈어요.
examples.en: The child opened and closed their mouth, imitating a fish.
The carp gaped its mouth, begging for food.

examples.ko: 물 밖으로 나온 물고기가 계속 뻐끔거려요.
examples.en: The fish that came out of the water keeps gasping.

examples.ko: 입만 뻐끔거릴 뿐 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: I only opened and closed my mouth, and no words came out.

explain: 물고기가 물속에서 입을 열었다 닫았다 하는 모습이 기본이에요. 사람에게 쓰면 소리는 안 나고 입 모양만 움직이는 모습이라서, 말소리가 들리는 '중얼거리다'와 달라요. 놀라거나 당황해서 말이 안 나올 때 비유로도 써요. '뻐끔대다'도 같은 말이에요.
explain_en: Its core image is a fish opening and closing its mouth in the water. For people it means the mouth moves with no sound coming out, unlike '중얼거리다' (to mumble), where you can hear words. It is also used figuratively when someone is too shocked or flustered to speak. '뻐끔대다' is the same word.

examples.en: My younger sibling goes in and out of the library all the time these days.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 우리 집에 뻔질나게 찾아와요.
examples.en: That person keeps turning up at our house.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 친구와 놀이터를 뻔질나게 다녔어요.
examples.en: When we were kids, my friend and I went to the playground all the time.

examples.ko: 왜 그 가게에 그렇게 뻔질나게 가요?
examples.en: Why do you go to that shop so often?
The friend who used to contact me constantly has gone quiet lately.

examples.ko: 아버지는 출장 때문에 공항을 뻔질나게 오가세요.
examples.en: My father goes back and forth to the airport all the time because of business trips.

explain: '자주'보다 말맛이 강해서, 어떤 곳을 쉴 새 없이 드나드는 모습에 써요. 보통 '뻔질나게' 꼴로 '드나들다, 다니다, 찾아오다' 같은 말과 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It has a stronger flavor than '자주' (often) and describes going somewhere again and again without a break. It usually appears as '뻔질나게' together with verbs like '드나들다', '다니다' and '찾아오다'.

examples.ko: 아기가 엄마 품에서 소르르 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: The baby drifted off to sleep in her mother's arms.
I'm sleepy and my eyes are slowly closing.
The ribbon came undone smoothly and the gift opened.
The ice melted away gently in the warm sunshine.
The sand slipped softly through my fingers.
The hem of the skirt slid down softly.

explain: '잠들다, 졸리다, 풀리다, 녹다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 가볍고 부드럽게 일어나는 일을 그릴 때 어울려요. 같은 뜻의 '스르르'가 큰말이라서, '소르르'는 조금 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It goes with words like '잠들다', '졸리다', '풀리다' and '녹다', and fits things that happen lightly and gently. '스르르' is the larger-sounding counterpart, so '소르르' feels a little smaller and lighter.

examples.en: The kids were whispering at the back of the classroom.

examples.ko: 사람들이 나를 보며 수군대는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems like people are whispering while looking at me.
Don't whisper behind my back, say it to me directly.

examples.ko: 둘이 귀에 대고 뭔가를 수군대고 있어요.
examples.en: The two of them are whispering something into each other's ears.

examples.ko: 회사 사람들이 그 소문을 두고 수군대요.
examples.en: People at the company are whispering about that rumor.
When I walked in, the staff started whispering.

explain: '수군거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 여럿이 작은 소리로 남의 이야기를 하는 느낌이 강해요. 다정하게 말하는 '속삭이다'와 달리 소문이나 험담처럼 부정적인 장면에 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It means the same as '수군거리다' and suggests several people talking quietly about someone else. Unlike the gentler '속삭이다' (to whisper), it often fits negative scenes such as rumors or gossip.

examples.en: The classroom buzzed at the sudden news.
People started to murmur restlessly.

examples.ko: 선거 결과가 나오자 회사 분위기가 술렁거려요.
examples.en: The mood at the company is unsettled now that the election results are out.
I don't know why everyone is so restless.
The buzzing audience quickly became quiet.
My mind was stirred up, so I couldn't sleep.

explain: '술렁이다', '술렁대다'와 뜻이 거의 같아요. 사람들이 놀라거나 불안하거나 들떠서 웅성웅성할 때 써요. 마음에도 쓸 수 있지만 보통은 모인 사람들이나 분위기에 써요.
explain_en: It means almost the same as '술렁이다' and '술렁대다'. It is used when people are surprised, anxious or excited and start to murmur. It can describe a mind too, but usually it describes a crowd or an atmosphere.

examples.en: A stray cat prowls the alley every evening.

examples.ko: 일요일 오후에 동네를 어슬렁거리다가 빵집에 들렀어요.
examples.en: On Sunday afternoon, I wandered around the neighborhood and stopped by a bakery.

examples.ko: 할 일이 없어서 집 앞을 어슬렁거렸어요.
examples.en: I had nothing to do, so I loitered in front of my house.
I strolled around the market with a friend, looking at things.

examples.ko: 아저씨가 가게 앞에서 어슬렁거리는 모습이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a man hanging around in front of the shop.
Don't dawdle; get ready quickly.

explain: '산책하다'는 일부러 걷는 것이지만 '어슬렁거리다'는 목적 없이 느릿느릿 돌아다니는 모습이에요. 한가하고 할 일 없는 느낌이 있고, 수상하게 서성이는 사람에게도 써요. '어슬렁대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: '산책하다' means walking on purpose, while '어슬렁거리다' means moving around slowly with no aim. It gives a feeling of idling or having nothing to do, and it is also used for someone loitering suspiciously. '어슬렁대다' is used with the same meaning.

examples.en: The puppy is wandering around in front of the door.

examples.ko: 할 일 없이 집 앞에서 어슬렁어슬렁하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't hang around in front of the house with nothing to do.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 아까부터 가게 앞을 어슬렁어슬렁했어요.
examples.en: That person has been loitering in front of the shop since a while ago.

examples.ko: 방학이라 하루 종일 집 안에서 어슬렁어슬렁하고 있어요.
examples.en: It's vacation, so I'm just lazing around the house all day.

examples.ko: 수상한 사람이 골목에서 어슬렁어슬렁하는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a suspicious person lurking around in the alley.

examples.ko: 약속 시간 전에 역 근처를 어슬렁어슬렁해도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: It's fine to stroll around the station before our meeting time.

explain: '어슬렁어슬렁'에 '하다'가 붙은 동사로, 목적 없이 천천히 돌아다닐 때 써요. '어슬렁거리다', '어슬렁대다'처럼 말하기도 해요. 상황에 따라 한가로운 느낌도 되고, 수상하게 서성이는 느낌도 돼요.
explain_en: This verb comes from '어슬렁어슬렁' and is used when someone walks around slowly without a purpose. People also say '어슬렁거리다' or '어슬렁대다'. Depending on the situation it can feel relaxed or like someone loitering suspiciously.

en: volunteer; do of one's own accord

examples.en: I volunteered to do the presentation.
The culprit came to the police station of his own accord.

examples.ko: 아무도 자진해 나서지 않아서 제비뽑기를 했어요.
examples.en: Nobody stepped forward, so we drew lots.
He took responsibility of his own accord.
We decided to give a prize to those who volunteer.
I was grateful that my coworker offered to help.

explain: 거의 '자진해서' 모양으로 써요. 누가 시키지 않았는데 스스로 나선다는 느낌이에요. '자원하다'는 일이나 봉사에 나설 때 쓰고, '자진해서'는 발표, 신고, 사과, 책임처럼 폭넓게 어울려요. 명사 '자진'은 '자진 신고'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙어요.
explain_en: It appears almost always as 자진해서, meaning stepping up without being told. 자원하다 is for volunteering for work or service, while 자진해서 fits a wider range, such as a presentation, reporting, apologizing or taking responsibility. The noun 자진 attaches before another word, as in 자진 신고.

examples.ko: 교실 여기저기서 킥킥거리며 웃음을 참는 소리가 났어요.
examples.en: Here and there in the classroom people were snickering, holding back laughter.
My friend saw my mistake and is snickering.
What's so funny that you're giggling?
The two of them whispered and giggled.
You shouldn't giggle during class.
The giggling kids made the teacher laugh too.

explain: 웃음을 참으면서 낮게 웃는 모습이에요. 재미있어서 웃을 때도 쓰지만, 놀리듯이 웃을 때도 써요. '킥킥대다'라고도 하고, 뜻은 거의 같아요.
explain_en: It describes laughing low while trying to hold it in. It is used for laughing at something funny, but also for laughing in a teasing way. People also say '킥킥대다', with almost the same meaning.

examples.ko: 동생이 내 얼굴을 보더니 히죽 웃었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling looked at my face and grinned.

examples.ko: 그는 아무 말 없이 히죽 웃기만 했어요.
examples.en: He just grinned without saying a word.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 들은 아이가 히죽 하고 웃었어요.
examples.en: The child who was praised let out a grin.

examples.ko: 혼자 히죽 웃는 걸 보니 좋은 일이 있나 봐요.
examples.en: Seeing you grinning to yourself, something good must have happened.

examples.ko: 친구가 히죽이 웃는 얼굴로 한마디 했어요.
examples.en: My friend said a word with a grin on his face.

examples.ko: 히죽 웃고 있는 친구에게 무슨 일이냐고 물었어요.
examples.en: I asked my grinning friend what was going on.

explain: 입을 한쪽으로 살짝 벌리고 흐뭇하거나 능글맞게 웃는 모습이에요. '빙긋'보다 속없어 보이거나 장난스러운 느낌이 있어요. 센 느낌의 '히쭉'도 있고, 계속 웃을 때는 '히죽히죽'을 써요.
explain_en: It shows a smile with the mouth opening slightly, either contentedly or slyly. Compared with '빙긋', it can seem a bit goofy or mischievous. There is also the stronger '히쭉', and '히죽히죽' is used when someone keeps grinning.
